userStories.title: Chain guidance in job notices and provider instructions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the pure workflow prompt builders with chain job notices and three fixed chain instruction lines while preserving all existing text.

**Motivation** — After feature 2, the session can start each billed step, but every step needs its own card.

**Approach** — **Notices.** The feature 2 job notice gains a third line for a chain job, telling the agent to read the chain's state with `nax-jobs__list`. The provider's instruction text gains three lines. Both are prompts, so they come from `src/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts`.

`JobNoticeInput` adds `readonly chainId?: string; readonly chainStep?: number`. With `chainId` set, the notice has a third line; without it, the output is unchanged.

**Notice and instruction text**
`buildJobNotice` third line for a job with `chainId` and `chainStep`:

`This job is step <chainStep> of chain <chainId>; call nax-jobs__list to see whether the chain continues, and if it does, call the next step's launch tool with exactly the approved arguments (no card is shown for it).`

`buildJobsInstructions` keeps its five lines, then adds:
1. `nax-jobs__chain` proposes a full run: an ordered list of billed steps on one approval card. Only the user's yes on that card approves it; a chat message such as "go ahead" does not.`
2. `While a chain is active, call each step's launch tool with exactly the approved arguments, one step at a time, after the previous step succeeded; a different call stops the chain and shows a normal card.`
3. `Before a step that names a check, run that check yourself and record its verdict with `nax-jobs__chain_check`; stop the chain with `nax-jobs__chain_stop` when the user asks.`

Preserve both original notice lines and the five original jobs instruction lines verbatim. Existing runner call sites already pass the full record, including any new optional fields, to this builder.

**Scope** — In: workflow-builder.ts additions and new workflow-builder-chain.test.ts. Out: any controller/provider/runner execution logic (US-001/002/003/004/006/007/008/009) and changing buildWorkflowInstructions.
- Making the chain line of a job notice depend on the chain still being current; a notice for a re-attached chain job in a later chat still names its chain, and `nax-jobs__list` then shows that chat's own chain or `null`.
- A chain view, footer marker or `/jobs` line in the TUI; the chain shows through its card, the tool results, the job notices and `nax-jobs__list`.

**Interface** —
```ts
// Add to JobNoticeInput:
readonly chainId?: string;
readonly chainStep?: number;

export function buildJobNotice(input: JobNoticeInput): string;
export function buildJobsInstructions(): string;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildJobNotice for a job with chainId chain-1a2b3c4d and chainStep 2 returns three lines.

[unit] The third line of that notice is This job is step 2 of chain chain-1a2b3c4d; call nax-jobs__list to see whether the chain continues, and if it does, call the next step's launch tool with exactly the approved arguments (no card is shown for it).
[unit] buildJobNotice for a job with no chainId returns two lines.

[unit] buildJobsInstructions() contains the line `nax-jobs__chain` proposes a full run: an ordered list of billed steps on one approval card. Only the user's yes on that card approves it; a chat message such as "go ahead" does not.

[unit] buildJobsInstructions() contains the line While a chain is active, call each step's launch tool with exactly the approved arguments, one step at a time, after the previous step succeeded; a different call stops the chain and shows a normal card.

[unit] buildJobsInstructions() contains the line Before a step that names a check, run that check yourself and record its verdict with `nax-jobs__chain_check`; stop the chain with `nax-jobs__chain_stop` when the user asks.
[unit] The fifth line of buildJobsInstructions() is still Start one step at a time: after a job ends, report the outcome to the user and propose the single next step.
[unit] buildJobsInstructions() returns eight lines.

[unit] When buildJobNotice receives { id: "run-1a2b3c4d", kind: "run", target: "f1", state: "failed", note: "no run record for pid 4242", logPath: "/o/l.log" } with no chainId, it returns exactly "[nax-jobs] job run-1a2b3c4d (run f1) ended: failed (no run record for pid 4242) log /o/l.log\nCall `nax-workflow__state`, report the outcome to the user and propose the single next step.", preserving the original failure notice without a chain continuation line.

routing.reasoning: Pure additive string builder behavior with optional inputs and exact output assertions; no permission, session or launch decision is implemented.

userStories.title: Register chain tools and validate chain proposals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add optional chain tool registration and validate the complete proposal before showing any approval card.

**Motivation** — A plain chat message such as "go ahead" is not an approval.

**Approach** — `createChainTools({ ...JobsProviderOptions, chains })` in `chain-tools.ts` returns three `ProviderTool`s. `createJobsProvider` appends them after `cancel` when `options.chains` is set. With chains absent, keep the existing six tools. `jobs-provider.ts` (114 lines) gains only the registration of the three tools, and the tools live in `chain-tools.ts`.

**`chain`.** Input schema: `{ steps: array of { kind: string, input: object, checkBefore?: string }, costCap?: number }`, `required: ["steps"]`, `additionalProperties: false`. Validation, in this order, with no card on any error:
1. `chains.active()` is defined: `[chat] chain <id> is already active; stop it with nax-jobs__chain_stop first`;
2. `steps` is not an array of 1 to `CHAIN_MAX_STEPS` items: `[chat] a chain needs 1 to 6 steps`;
3. `costCap` is present and not a positive finite number: `[chat] costCap must be a positive number`;
4. per step N, in order: a step that is not an object, or whose `input` is missing or is not a plain object (null and arrays included), gives `[chat] step N: input must be an object`; a `kind` that is not one of the four launch kinds (a non-string included) gives `[chat] step N: unknown kind <kind>`; a `parseChainStepInput` error (an unknown input field included) gives `[chat] step N: <error without its [chat] prefix>`; a `checkBefore` that is not a string of 1 to `CHAIN_CHECK_MAX_LENGTH` characters gives `[chat] step N: checkBefore must be 1 to 200 characters`;
5. per plan step N, `resolvePlanSpec` resolves the spec (the feature 2 candidate order); its error gives `[chat] step N: <error without its [chat] prefix>`, for example `[chat] step N: no spec for <feature>; looked for <paths>`. Run and bot steps get no target check at chain time; their launch call runs the full feature 2 preparation.

After validation, build exact argv through buildChainStepArgv, storing prIndex only for PR-less bot steps and target as feature name, explicit PR decimal string or empty string. Preserve which plan PRDs already exist for US-008's warning lines. Never prepareRun at chain time: plan → run may not yet have prd.json. Valid proposals must reach approve so the boundary AC is executable; complete card text and activation belong to US-008. chain_check and chain_stop may be minimal here with final tool names/schemas, and are completed in US-009.

**Scope** — In: new chain-tools.ts, registration in jobs-provider.ts, chain schema/ordered validation and resolved steps, new chain-tool-input.test.ts using a real controller with temp output dir and fixture .nax/features/f1/spec.md/prd.json. Out: complete card text/approval activation (US-008), functional chain_check/chain_stop and list/host wiring (US-009), controller transitions (US-004), and running checks or launching steps.
- Any merge, release, `nax workflow promote` or ruling-post step in a chain; a chain only holds `nax plan`, `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix` steps, and it ends at a PR that is ready or draft.
- Giving subagent sessions the chain tools; like every `nax-jobs` tool, they reach the parent chat only.
- Registering the chain tools in the ACP server (koda); only `nax chat` gets them.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function createChainTools(options: JobsProviderOptions & { readonly chains: ChatChains }): ProviderTool[];
```
The provider tool schemas use ProviderTool and ToolResult from @nathapp/nax-agent, and the host approval port remains JobsProviderOptions.approve.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With chains set, awaiting createJobsProvider(options).tools(options.repoRoot) returns tools whose local names are ["plan", "run", "bot_review", "bot_fix", "list", "cancel", "chain", "chain_check", "chain_stop"].
[unit] The chain tool's input schema has required ["steps"] and additionalProperties false.
[unit] A nax-jobs__chain call with steps: [] returns the error [chat] a chain needs 1 to 6 steps.
[unit] A nax-jobs__chain call with seven valid run steps returns the error [chat] a chain needs 1 to 6 steps.
[unit] A nax-jobs__chain call with six valid run steps and a 200-character checkBefore on step 2 reaches approve.
[unit] A nax-jobs__chain call whose steps is the string "plan" returns the error [chat] a chain needs 1 to 6 steps.
[unit] A step that is the string "run" returns the error [chat] step 1: input must be an object.
[unit] A step { kind: "run" } with no input returns the error [chat] step 1: input must be an object.
[unit] A step whose input is an array returns the error [chat] step 1: input must be an object.
[unit] A step with kind merge returns the error [chat] step 1: unknown kind merge.
[unit] A step with kind 7 returns the error [chat] step 1: unknown kind 7.
[unit] A run step with input { feature: "f1", bogus: 1 } returns the error [chat] step 1: unknown field bogus.

[unit] A run step with feature ../x returns an error whose content equals "[chat] step 1: " followed by the error message parseJobInput("run", { feature: "../x" }) returns, with that message's leading "[chat] " removed.
[unit] A plan step for feature f9, which has no spec, returns an error starting [chat] step 1: no spec for f9; looked for.
[unit] costCap -1 returns the error [chat] costCap must be a positive number.
[unit] costCap "10" (a string) returns the error [chat] costCap must be a positive number.
[unit] A step 2 with checkBefore "" returns the error [chat] step 2: checkBefore must be 1 to 200 characters.
[unit] A step 2 with a 201-character checkBefore returns the error [chat] step 2: checkBefore must be 1 to 200 characters.
[unit] A nax-jobs__chain call while a chain is active returns the error [chat] chain <id> is already active; stop it with nax-jobs__chain_stop first.
[unit] When a chain is active and the step list is also empty, the error is the already-active error.
[unit] For each invalid call above, the stub approve is never called.
[unit] When a step's input is null or otherwise not a plain object, nax-jobs__chain returns [chat] step N: input must be an object without showing a card.
[unit] With options.chains absent, awaiting createJobsProvider(options).tools(options.repoRoot) returns the unchanged local-name list ["plan", "run", "bot_review", "bot_fix", "list", "cancel"].

routing.reasoning: Two source files add standard provider registration and ordered validation using existing argv/spec/controller ports; exact approved-input validation is security-critical despite the bounded medium scope.

suggestedCriteria: When costCap is 0, NaN or Infinity, the chain tool returns [chat] costCap must be a positive number without calling approve.
When checkBefore is a number, the chain tool returns [chat] step N: checkBefore must be 1 to 200 characters without calling approve.
When a plan step has a resolvable spec and its following run step has no prd.json yet, proposal validation still reaches approve.

userStories.title: Full-run card, explicit approval and durable activation
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] A nax-jobs__chain call with steps plan f1 and run f1 with maxIterations 40 calls approve once with tool nax-jobs__chain.
[unit] For that call, the card command equals the plan step's argv joined by spaces, a newline, and the run step's argv joined by spaces.
[unit] For that call, the card summary is full run of 2 steps: nax plan f1 → nax run f1.
[unit] For that call, the card reason contains the line 1. nax plan f1 — starts after: you approve this card.
[unit] For that call, the card reason contains the line 2. nax run f1 — starts after: step 1 succeeded.

[unit] Without costCap, the card reason contains no cost cap.

[unit] With the interaction plugin cli and a run step in the chain, the card reason contains warning: run steps have no channel for their own asks; they will time out.

[unit] For a single bot_review step without pr, the card summary is full run of 1 steps: nax bot review (PR chosen by the agent).

When git branch lookup fails, the card's first reason line is workdir <repoRoot> without a branch suffix.

userStories.title: Check/stop tools, chain listing and parent chat composition
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish chain_check and chain_stop, expose chain summaries in list, and compose the real controller into parent chat jobs and close confirmation.

**Motivation** — The main nax roadmap is one `nax chat` session that takes the user from a brainstorm to an open PR (user, 2026-10-24).

**Approach** — **`chain_check`.** Input `{ step: integer, passed: boolean, note: string }`, all required. Calls `chains.recordCheck`. `{ ok: false, message }` gives error `[chat] <message>`. `{ ok: true }` gives `check recorded for step <step>`, plus `; the chain stopped` when `passed` was `false`.

**`chain_stop`.** Input `{}`. No card: stopping a chain only removes autonomy and never cancels a job. With an active chain: `chains.stop("stopped by the agent")`, result `chain <id> stopped; running jobs keep running`. Without one: error `[chat] no active chain`.

`createJobsProvider(options)` target: when `options.chains` is set, tools `plan, run, bot_review, bot_fix, list, cancel, chain, chain_check, chain_stop`, and `list` with no `job` returns `{ jobs, omitted, chain }`, where `chain` is `options.chains.summary()`. With no chains, preserve feature 2's exact tool list and listing shape. Do not add chain to a job-detail query.

`createHostJobs(options)` target: also builds `chains = createChainController({ outputDir, cwd: repoRoot, jobs, sessionId, now })`, passes it to `createJobsProvider`, returns `{ jobs, chains, provider, guard, confirmClose }`, and `confirmClose` first calls `chains.stop("the chat closed")`.

**Close.** `createHostJobs().confirmClose` stops the active chain with reason `the chat closed` before anything else, whether or not jobs are still running. A kept job keeps running in the background, and the chain does not start its next step (design 4.3). Preserve the existing single close approval when owned jobs run and no approval when none do.

The `src/chat/jobs/index.ts` barrel exports `createChainController` and the chain types. `chat-host.ts` (566 lines, held under the 600-line limit) does not change. Existing host wiring already provides the live session id closure, registers the jobs provider only in the parent and keeps host-owned cards pending even in full mode.

Seams to verify: a chain approved through the real `nax-jobs__chain` tool lets the real `nax-jobs__run` tool start step 1 with no second `approve` call (a real `createChainController`, a stub `jobs.start`); repeat the run call with a non-blocking stub running-job list to reach admission and assert a second `approve` call. From `createChatHost` with a `naxEntry`, the `nax-jobs` provider the session receives has the `chain`, `chain_check` and `chain_stop` tools, and a chain card raised in full mode stays in `host.asks.pending()` until resolved. Build host fixtures the way chat-host-jobs.test.ts does, without modifying that existing test file.

**Scope** — In: complete chain-tools.ts check/stop, conditionally extend list in jobs-provider.ts, controller composition/return/close stop in jobs-host.ts, barrel exports, new chain-tools.test.ts and chat-host-chain.test.ts. Out: launch policy changes (US-006), proposal/card behavior changes (US-007/008), and controller internals (US-002/003/004).
- Any change to `nax run`, `nax plan`, `nax bot`, `@nathapp/nax-agent` or `chat-host.ts`.
- Giving subagent sessions the chain tools; like every `nax-jobs` tool, they reach the parent chat only.
- Registering the chain tools in the ACP server (koda); only `nax chat` gets them.
- A chain view, footer marker or `/jobs` line in the TUI; the chain shows through its card, the tool results, the job notices and `nax-jobs__list`.
- Cancelling the running job when the chain stops or is stopped; `nax-jobs__cancel` (with its own card) cancels a job.
- Cross-session memory; it is its own slice, not yet designed (user ruling 2026-10-27).

**Interface** —
```ts
recordCheck(step: number, passed: boolean, note: string): { readonly ok: true } | { readonly ok: false; readonly message: string };
stop(reason: string): ChatChain | undefined;
/** The current chain (active, completed or stopped), or null before the first activation. */
summary(): ChainSummary | null;
```
createHostJobs extends its existing returned object with chains: ChatChains; no new member is required on createChatHost's public API.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] nax-jobs__chain_check with { step: 2, passed: true, note: "READY" } for a next step 2 that has a check returns check recorded for step 2.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_check with { step: 2, passed: false, note: "2 blockers" } returns check recorded for step 2; the chain stopped.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_check with no active chain returns the error [chat] no active chain.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_check for step 3 while step 2 is next returns the error [chat] step 3 is not the next step.
[unit] The chain_check input schema requires step, passed and note, with additionalProperties false.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_stop with an active chain returns chain <id> stopped; running jobs keep running, and chains.active() then returns undefined.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_stop never calls approve.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_stop with no active chain returns the error [chat] no active chain.
[unit] nax-jobs__list with no job and chains set returns JSON whose chain is null before any chain.
[unit] After a chain is activated, nax-jobs__list with no job returns JSON whose chain deep-equals chains.summary().

[integration] After a chain of one step, run f1, is approved through nax-jobs__chain (stub approve resolving allow), a nax-jobs__run call for f1 calls the stub jobs.start once with chainStep 1, and approve has been called once in total.
[integration] After that auto-started step, a second nax-jobs__run call for f1 calls approve again, so approve has been called twice in total.
[unit] createHostJobs(...) returns a chains member whose active() is undefined and whose summary() is null.
[unit] The provider returned by createHostJobs(...) has tools named chain, chain_check and chain_stop.
[unit] With an active chain and no owned running jobs, confirmClose() resolves without calling requestHostApproval, and chains.summary().stopReason is the chat closed.
[unit] With an active chain and one owned running job, confirmClose() stops the chain with stopReason the chat closed and calls requestHostApproval once.
[integration] From createChatHost with a naxEntry and resources, the nax-jobs provider passed to the session's open request has tools named chain, chain_check and chain_stop.
[integration] In a full-mode host from createChatHost, a nax-jobs__chain call for one run step of f1 leaves one ask in host.asks.pending() whose tool is nax-jobs__chain until it is resolved.
[unit] nax-jobs__chain_check for a next step N without checkBefore returns the error [chat] step N has no check to record.
[unit] With options.chains absent and jobs.list() returning [], nax-jobs__list with no job returns content exactly {"jobs":[],"omitted":0}, preserving the existing listing shape with no chain key.

routing.reasoning: Parent-session approval composition and revocation on close span host/provider/controller boundaries; strict security TDD verifies the real one-card launch seam and full-mode host asks.

suggestedCriteria: When chain_stop stops an active chain with a running job, the job remains running and jobs.cancel is not called.
When close confirmation is denied after stopping a chain, owned jobs remain running and the chain remains stopped.
When a new host sees persisted chain records from an earlier host, nax-jobs__list returns chain null until a new chain card is approved.

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to the shipped chat workflow state and dispatch features, entirely in packages/nax; it is not a new execution engine. Repository exploration used Read/Grep because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host. Architecture guidance was read at docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:1; its index requires dependency injection, structured NaxError errors, prompt builders and bounded modules (quick reference at :171). Use Bun, strict TypeScript, bun:test, existing @test/helpers and _deps seams; do not introduce dependencies or modify sibling packages.

Verified baseline and impact: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-types.ts:1 defines the four launch kinds and five job states; ChatJob at :5 has no chain fields and gains optional chainId/chainStep. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-argv.ts:7 defines JobLaunchInput, :131 parseJobInput validates feature names and delegates kind-specific parsing, and :150 buildJobArgv constructs token arrays without a shell. Bot PR parsing at :98 accepts positive safe integers, including numeric strings; chain parsing must reuse these semantics while rejecting unknown keys before delegation. A missing bot PR must be parsed using a valid temporary PR and then omitted from the returned object, not passed undefined to the existing required-PR parser. Profiles default to [], and optional false flags may normalize to the same argv. Authorization compares built argv token by token, not raw objects or joined display strings. The bot PR token is at naxEntry.length + 2; replace only that index so another '<pr>' token such as a decisions path remains unchanged. Explicit PRs remain exact; only omitted PRs participate in the chain's once-chosen PR binding.

Persistence model: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-store.ts:10 exposes _jobStoreDeps, :35 validates ids before writing a unique sibling temp file and renaming, :57 retains cleanup errors, :71 validates a minimum job record without projecting unknown fields away, and :88 treats missing/malformed JSON as absence while preserving unexpected I/O errors. Mirror these patterns in chain-store.ts, using CHAT_CHAIN_INVALID_ID and CHAT_CHAIN_WRITE_FAILED with stage 'chat' rather than copying the old 'chat-jobs' stage. The existing job reader already preserves new optional chain fields; it needs no migration or projection change. packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7 re-exports NaxError from nax-agent/internal; do not invent a new error registry or modify nax-agent. CHAT_CHAIN_ACTIVE is raised in the controller with stage 'chat'. Chain files are audit-only, schemaVersion 1, under outputDir/chat-chains; never rehydrate autonomy from them. Activation must await a successful durable record before exposing active state, and must reserve its in-flight activation slot synchronously so parallel approved cards cannot create two active chains. After activation, memory is authoritative and writes are best effort with getLogger()?.warn('chat', ...); avoid unhandled rejections and stale snapshots overwriting newer audit state.

Runner seam: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-runner.ts:20 defines StartJobRequest and :27 ChatJobs, including synchronous get and onChange plus asynchronous start. start at :130 spawns and registers before its first await, then spreads the request into the record at :145, so optional chain fields propagate without changing execution. onChange emission at :102 invokes listeners synchronously; start emits at :174 before the launch can call chains.started. Finalization sets a terminal record before emission and builds notices at :210. A job may finish before started links its id, so admit must reconcile terminal state directly through jobs.get even without a notification. Terminal outcomes, not exit codes, are authoritative: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-outcome.ts:35 only obtains cost for PID-matched run jobs, :43 derives run state from run artifacts, :71 resolves plan/bot outcomes. Sum recorded cost with missing cost as zero; no new plan/bot accounting. The cap stops subsequent steps only after successful job completion, never interrupts a running job, and final-step success completes before checking the cap. Controller onChange handling must be idempotent; dispose removes only its listener. summary applies session invalidation but must not opportunistically run job-end transitions, preserving the explicit dispose AC.

Launch integration: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts:85 prepares a plan by searching feature spec.md then .nax/specs/<feature>.md, or an explicit repo-relative spec, and checking existing prd.json. Extract that logic into resolvePlanSpec with unchanged messages and _jobsLaunchDeps.exists, and keep the existing replacement warning in preparePlan. :113 prepareRun reads/counts pending stories and builds warnings; add structured Prepared.overLimit beside the existing warning, never infer policy from warning text. :167 launchJob currently parses, prepares, applies early busyJob/busyLock at :177, builds argv, asks, then starts. Admit only after preparation and early busy checks: rejected preparation, an existing run/plan, or live lock must leave the chain unchanged. :51 startApproved awaits the late lock check, then performs the in-memory running-job check immediately before jobs.start. Extend that boundary with a synchronous chains.isActive(chainId) guard after all awaits; no await may separate this guard from jobs.start. Auto launches retain the original busy/spawn error text and report failures via startFailed with the [chat] prefix stripped. Over-limit auto runs stop the chain and fall back to an ordinary card. The original per-step path remains byte-for-byte compatible in output/card behavior when chains is absent, and chain keys must be omitted, not passed as undefined.

Provider/host seam: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.ts:10 defines options and gains optional chains; :61 inspectionTool handles list/cancel and :92 createJobsProvider currently registers six ordered tools. Append the three chain tools only when chains is present; list without a job conditionally adds chains.summary(), while detail/cancel schemas and behavior stay unchanged. Keep validation/card logic in chain-tools.ts to avoid growing the 114-line provider into a controller. packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:8 defines HostApprovalCard and :72 requestHostApproval creates expiring host-owned asks even in full mode. Abort and timeout resolve deny, and host approvals cannot be remembered (:135). A chain becomes active only after this port returns allow, never from chat text, permission memory or full mode. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:21 is the intended composition root: create the controller with repoRoot as cwd and the existing live sessionId closure, pass it into the provider, return it, and stop it before any close confirmation work at :36. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:149 already composes createHostJobs when both resources and naxEntry exist, :159 supplies () => this.current().sessionId, :176 gives subagents only resources.toolProviders, and :188 appends jobs only for the parent session. These existing connections provide chain tools to parent chat without changing chat-host.ts (566 lines). Its teardown at :538 disposes the job runner; feature close behavior is deliberately implemented in createHostJobs.confirmClose, not by changing chat-host.ts. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/index.ts:1 is the existing barrel to extend with controller/types. Consumers of ChatJob include packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts:4 and the chat barrel at packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:41; optional fields require no TUI or public-host changes.

Prompt ownership: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.ts:16 defines JobNoticeInput; :27 emits two-line notices; :37 returns five instruction lines. Add conditional chain notice text and append precisely the three specified instruction lines, leaving all original lines unchanged. packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts:133 already exports these builders. Both owned and attached runner notices pass full records, so no new notice router is needed. Reattached chain jobs may mention an old inert chain; list always describes only this host's controller.

Existing regression anchors and fixtures: packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-launch-busy.test.ts:35 builds options with temp PRD/spec and _jobsLaunchDeps stubs; :96 pins early busy rejection, :115 late job/lock races, :126 bot independence, :165 simultaneous launches. packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.test.ts:76 pins the six-tool order and :90 closed list/cancel schemas; its fixture has no chains, so it must remain unchanged. packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/job-store.test.ts:24 creates complete fixture records and :90 checks atomic replacement/cleanup; mirror it for the new store, keeping new tests in chain-store.test.ts. packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/workflow-builder.test.ts:127 pins two-line non-chain notices and :185 preserves existing instruction text. packages/nax/test/unit/chat/chat-host-jobs.test.ts:39 builds a real createChatHost using makeNaxConfig/makeLogger, a stub open request and runner spawn; :190 proves full-mode host cards remain pending, :219 pins close prompting and :247 disposal without cancellation. Additional existing suites include job-argv.test.ts, jobs-launch.test.ts, job-runner.test.ts, job-runner-attach.test.ts, job-runner-cancel.test.ts, job-outcome.test.ts and job-write-guard.test.ts. New tests must use the exact new filenames assigned to each story; no existing assertions need modification. The spec's 'Modifies: None' describes existing test assertions, not source edits: source extensions listed above are required.

Implementation order is binding: US-001 creates contracts/argv/store; US-002 activation/admission; US-003 checks/session/PR consistency; US-004 transitions/cost/summary. US-005 prompt changes is independent. US-006 depends exactly on US-002 and US-005 and integrates using a stub controller, without assuming US-003/004 already ran. US-007 validation depends on US-006; US-008 card/activation depends on US-007; US-009 depends on US-004 and US-008 and completes host/tool integration. Minimal controller/tool methods allowed in intermediate stories must retain the final public signatures and compile, with their behavior finished in the assigned downstream stories. Each context file exists now or is created by an upstream dependency. Every path is repo-rooted even though all workdirs are packages/nax.

Primary risks: unauthorized off-card launches, reusing approvals across sessions, double admission in the same tick, a stopped chain starting after asynchronous lock checks, duplicate terminal writes, PR wildcard substitution beyond its sole approved slot, and loss of prepared warnings on the auto path. Preserve admission order exactly: terminal reconciliation, session, exact kind/argv, bound PR, previous succeeded record, passed named check; reservation is synchronous. Stop is irreversible and never cancels work. Match error text and card line order as part of the tool protocol. There is no database migration, version bump, record backfill or new config. Existing job records remain readable; new chains are opt-in via an explicit card and never resume from disk. Validate through new targeted bun:test files from packages/nax; never run bare bun test or bun run nax. Pipeline handles lint/typecheck/tests; do not run coverage inside a sandboxed nax session. Routing uses strict three-session-tdd for the approval/admission/session/access-control stories; the pure prompt and record/argv additions use tdd-simple. Suggested criteria are separate from required spec ACs; required failure-table rows not already represented by a listed AC are included in the matching story.

Refine-pass audit: re-read the stored spec, the draft, jobs-launch.ts, jobs-provider.ts, jobs-host.ts, workflow-builder.ts, ask-controller.ts, job-store.ts, job-runner.ts and provider regression tests. The spec has 169 explicitly listed ACs: US-001 21, US-002 21, US-003 20, US-004 19, US-005 8, US-006 21, US-007 21, US-008 20, US-009 18. Each remains in acceptanceCriteria of its original story, in the same ordinal position; additional failure-table/regression assertions follow the originals. No source AC uses a deprecated grep/file/verbatim tag. All clauses such as 'with no pr key', 'for that input', 'still <pr>', 'never fired', 'unchanged', 'already holding', 'in total' and 'until it is resolved' were retained. Corrections preserve semantic intent: endedAt is now().toISOString(), not a Date object; provider.tools is awaited with repoRoot and its localName values are projected; the repeated-admit off-card scenario explicitly uses one step so it cannot be confused with a legal next step having identical argv; the invalid-feature error criterion preserves the exact leading '[chat] ' space removal.

Exhaustive AC preservation ledger (numbers are the spec's within-story ordinals, mapped to the same PRD ordinals):

New failed-notice, optional-provider and optional-list regressions fit their existing source/test scope, without adding stories or files. No production code was changed during this PRD audit.
outOfScope: Any merge, release, `nax workflow promote` or ruling-post step in a chain; a chain only holds `nax plan`, `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix` steps, and it ends at a PR that is ready or draft.
Restarting, resuming or editing a chain once it has stopped or completed; a new chain needs a new card.

Reading chain records back into an active chain after a restart, a `--resume` or a crash; a chain never outlives the chat host that approved it, and a record left `active` on disk by a crash is inert.
Checking the cost cap while a step runs, or killing a running step when the cap is passed; the cap is checked only when a step ends, and a run step's own `--max-cost` bounds spend inside that step.
Counting the cost of plan and bot jobs toward the cap; only `run` jobs record cost.
